title: Direct reach at every depth: blocks of orbits and a block's descent
claim: Theorem W: the blocks of the maps' orbits (an orbit with its children) meet only parent to child, so with orbits of bounded size ties, two-orbit three-member bonds and life are decided at every depth by a finite computation; computed: of population D, 10 constant-2 descriptions have L = 2 and 32 constant-3 descriptions L = 3 exactly at every depth and every s, and 43 half-rate ones no tie at any depth. Theorem D: a few addresses followed down one letter each (eventually periodic) carry ties (D1) or three-member bonds (D2) to every depth; with finite-reader states, 15 of 34 constant-2 descriptions have L = 2 and 39 of 66 constant-3 descriptions L <= 3 at every depth. Referee pending.
failure_conditions: A description with orbits of at most four addresses where the block computation disagrees with SAT at some depth.
A descent whose claimed tie or constrained triple fails in the whole pattern at some depth.
A finite-reader state that violates a knot at some level.
remaining_obligations: Constant-2 descriptions with growing orbits: 19 of 34 open.
Exact L = 3 at every depth with growing orbits: open (D2 gives L <= 3 only).
foundation_claim_scope: The plain not-all-equal law; addressed patterns placed by automaton maps, knots within a level or between adjacent levels.

validation.independence: Written by Claude 2026-11-16 (code by the thread, validated against Codex-built certified SAT results of 001A); advisor checked the arguments; referee pending.
validation.status: proof by hand plus finite computation; check passed
